machines.name: A referral destination
machines.subject: One addressed destination. A referral can name several distinct wards within the configured recipient cap; answers and reassessments belong to the individual destination.

states.label: Waiting
states.sub: Doing nothing is a real answer, and the commonest one. It stays here indefinitely.

states.label: Accepted
states.sub: Records a destination answer. Acceptance creates no movement or admission; a ward answer may also reserve a named bed on the referral.

states.label: Declined
states.sub: Ends this answer. An explicit clinical reassessment can reconsider a declined destination.

states.label: Cancelled
states.sub: Closed automatically because another destination accepted. Nobody is asked.

states.label: Withdrawn — a flag, not a state
states.sub: Stamped on every destination still waiting. The arm stays waiting; it does not end.

transitions.guard: the reason must come from this destination kind's own list

transitions.label: on clinical reassessment
transitions.guard: only as an explicit clinical reassessment of this destination

transitions.label: another arm accepted
transitions.guard: a community arm is exempt in both directions and is never cancelled
refused once anything is accepted, and refused outright once transport has collected the patient
transitions.label: stamps every waiting arm

machines.note: The destination states remain queued, accepted, declined and cancelled. A withdrawal stamps still-queued arms without rewriting their state. A clinical reassessment can update an accepted answer or turn a decline into acceptance; the ordinary first-acceptance cancellation excludes community arms in both directions.

machines.name: A movement
machines.subject: The separate bed-search record created by RAISE_REFERRAL, or created already arrived by an admitted-ward transfer. Front-door acceptance alone creates no movement. Seven stages plus a separate closure.

states.label: Placement requested
states.sub: Wards can be asked from here.

states.label: Destination review
states.sub: Wards can be asked from here too — and only from these two.

states.label: Accepted, awaiting bed
states.sub: A ward has said yes. No bed is set aside.

states.label: Bed pulled
states.sub: A bed is pulled and linked to an admission. The hold uses current configuration and any applicable extra-travel extension; expiry flags it for a person rather than releasing it.

states.label: Handover ready
states.sub: Requires a booked job or an explicitly recorded no-transport-needed answer, plus current held-bed gender and legal checks.

states.label: Moving
states.sub: The patient is in the vehicle.

states.label: Arrived
states.sub: STEP_BACK_STAGE cannot reverse arrival. A separate scoped Undo may reverse the latest unchanged recorded arrival within its window and restored-bed checks.

states.label: Closed — did not proceed
states.sub: Not a stage. The stage it closed at is still recorded.

transitions.label: a ward says no
transitions.guard: that ward drops off the list; the stage does not move

Allowed while awaiting a bed or with a pulled/stepped-back hold. A held bed is released atomically; cancel a live transport job first. Refused at handover-ready/moving. The referral's answer at that ward goes back to waiting (H3).
refused while a revoked examination still holds the bed, or while restrictive practice is still recorded as in use for the patient at the sending ward

transitions.label: community order or revoked
transitions.guard: A community order before transport commitment closes and refunds. Revocation while a bed is held retains it and flags release; commitment or collection also retains the bed.
the bed deliberately stays held; only releasing the held bed gives it back

transitions.label: closes as arrived, not as did-not-proceed
ward transfer arrival: created already arrived
transitions.guard: only a coordinator recording a transfer as arrived, for an occupied admission, into a ward with a suitable free bed and staffing; the new movement is opened and closed as arrived in one write, never raised in a department

transitions.label: to ANY strictly earlier stage
transitions.guard: refused once arrived; touches nothing but the stage — no bed given back, no transport cancelled
the same step back as from Moving: to any strictly earlier stage, touching nothing but the stage
the same step back as from Moving: to any strictly earlier stage, touching nothing but the stage
the same step back as from Moving: to any strictly earlier stage, touching nothing but the stage
the same step back as from Moving: to any strictly earlier stage, touching nothing but the stage
the held bed is released in the same write; cancel a live transport job first The referral's answer at that ward goes back to waiting (H3).

transitions.label: community order
transitions.guard: a community order before a bed is pulled closes the journey

transitions.label: community order
transitions.guard: a community order before a bed is pulled closes the journey

transitions.label: community order
transitions.guard: a community order before a bed is pulled closes the journey

machines.note: STEP_BACK_STAGE records a strictly earlier stage with a reason, leaving bed and transport intact. It refuses a closure, an arrived stage or a delivered transport leg. WITHDRAW_ACCEPTANCE can release an uncollected hold atomically after cancelling a live job. The separate scoped UNDO_TRANSPORT_STEP route may reverse the latest recorded arrival while its time-window, unchanged-snapshot, actor and restored-bed checks pass. Withdrawing the referral (after placement is requested), an ED outcome (before Moving) and a community order (before a bed is pulled) close the movement from every open stage the engine allows, not only from Bed pulled; tests/ward-audit-m26-machine-moves.test.ts checks every arrow against the engine.

machines.name: An admission
machines.subject: The held or occupied stay. A new pull creates a held admission; supported direct placement/planned-arrival and ward-transfer paths, and an arrival for a journey with no pulled stay, can create an occupied admission without passing through Held.

states.label: Held
states.sub: A bed is theirs. They are not here yet.

states.label: Occupied
states.sub: Stays theirs through leave, an ED trip, and an absconding.

states.label: Departed
states.sub: Kept. Ended, never deleted.

states.label: Removed — not a state
states.sub: There is no “deleted” among the four admission states. The record itself is taken away.

states.label: Waitlisted
states.sub: No action in the engine can produce this. Only the starting fixture writes it.

transitions.guard: only from occupied, and only by the ward they are on

transitions.label: transferred to another ward
transitions.guard: only when a coordinator records the transfer as arrived; the stay ends with the destination transferred-to-another-psychiatric-ward and any live bed release is completed

transitions.label: transfer arrival: new admission, already occupied
transitions.guard: the receiving ward gets a NEW admission with a new linked movement; no bed is pulled first, so it never passes through Held

transitions.label: away at an ED — bed untouched

machines.note: Ending and deleting are deliberately different. A departed admission is kept as a record that somebody was here; a released pull is removed, because the claim that they would be here is being retracted.

machines.name: A transport job
machines.subject: Booked by phone and logged here. Collection is the line that changes what is possible.

states.label: Collected
states.sub: After this, cancelling is impossible.

states.label: Stopped
states.sub: Somebody must say where the patient now is.

transitions.guard: five answers, none defaulted

Requires an open movement at handover-ready, an accepted job and no earlier en-route timestamp. Refused while a revoked/community-order examination retains a bed or awaits release; this handler itself does not rerun held-unit gender/legal checks.
refused while restrictive practice is still recorded as in use for the patient at the sending ward

transitions.label: the job is deleted, not marked

transitions.guard: The booking ward/team must match the supplied acting place; an ED claim is checked against the recorded booking place when both are present. Coordinator access remains subject to the authenticated access boundary.

machines.note: Cancel and stop are not two names for one thing. Cancel deletes a job before collection and leaves the bed held; stop ends a journey already underway, closes the movement, and also leaves the bed held — but only stop demands to know where the patient is.

machines.name: A bed release
machines.subject: A ward's plan for a bed coming free. It names the stay it belongs to, and nothing else about the person leaving.

states.label: Expected
states.sub: Carries what it is waiting on — one of seven.

states.label: Confirmed
states.sub: Decided. Still not a free bed.

states.label: Discharged
states.sub: The only step here that moves a real bed count.

states.label: Stuck — a flag, not a stage
states.sub: One of nine reasons. Sits on top of expected or confirmed; either can be flagged.

states.label: Being made ready — a flag
states.sub: Cleaning or repair is a separate flag. It can be set on an expected, confirmed or discharged release, and recording the departure (or a ward transfer arriving) sets it too, except item 18's "Left the ward, waiting for transport", where the bed is Ready at once. It does not rewrite the ward count, and a bed still being made ready may still be pulled (D-181 item 5).

transitions.label: the patient's ward transfer completes it
straight from expected, by ward transfer
made ready after the person leaves
the departure also marks the bed, unless left waiting for transport
the departure also marks the bed, unless left waiting for transport
a ward transfer arriving also marks the bed
a ward transfer arriving also marks the bed

machines.note: Being stuck used to be a fourth stage and was deliberately removed on 28 August 2026, because each stage says only how certain the discharge is. Stuck-ness and cleaning are two separate flags sitting on top.

machines.name: The front door — an expect becomes a referral
machines.subject: A door the earlier drawing missed entirely. A referral that has been triaged but whose patient has not arrived sits on a separate list; marking them present is what moves it.

states.label: Expected to arrive
states.sub: Triaged, and the patient is not here yet. It sits on the Expects list.

states.label: In the department
states.sub: Marked present. It now reads as a referral rather than an expect.

states.label: Medically cleared — or not
states.sub: Three answers, not two: unrecorded, cleared, and explicitly not cleared.

transitions.guard: stamped once; a repeat keeps the earliest time

machines.note: The owner's own words for this, quoted in the model: “When expects arrive and are marked as arrived, they become referrals.” Being marked present is the only door between the two lists.

machines.name: A patient's legal status
machines.subject: Four values on an open movement. CHANGE_LEGAL_STATUS records a change and history; it does not itself release a bed or advance the journey. Sending-desk kind and authenticated place scope still apply.
machines.note: Any value can be recorded as another; arrows illustrate examples rather than an enforced legal sequence. The handler requires a listed reason and an open movement. A newly unsuitable accepted ward is surfaced for a person; forward placement/transport steps recheck legal authority, so the change can block later progress.

machines.name: An examination
machines.subject: Four outcomes. Two of them end the bed search; one of them asks for another examination and is the only way a second one is allowed.

states.label: Further examination ordered
states.sub: The only outcome that allows another examination.

states.label: Inpatient order
states.sub: Recorded. Nothing else changes.

states.label: Community order, or revoked
states.sub: A community order or revocation is recorded. Closure/release depends on the held-bed and transport facts.

states.label: Superseded
states.sub: The previous examination is kept, not overwritten.

transitions.label: a second examination
transitions.guard: a second examination is refused unless the last one ordered a further one

machines.note: A community order before transport commitment closes the search and releases its hold. Revocation with a held bed retains the bed and admission, keeps the movement open and flags a person to act. At handover-ready, moving or after collection either ending outcome also retains it. Acceptance, en-route and collection refuse an unresolved examination/hold; physical arrival remains recordable.

machines.name: A notice
machines.subject: Twenty-four kinds of message, addressed to one role at one place. Written once, never rewritten, never deleted and never expiring.

states.label: Raised, unread
states.sub: Its wording is frozen at the moment it is written, even if the thing it describes later changes.

states.label: Read
states.sub: Only the addressee can mark it, only by clicking, and only once.

transitions.label: one of twenty-four kinds
transitions.guard: raised as a side-effect of an action, never on its own
refused if you are not the addressee, and refused a second time

machines.note: Opening the drawer does not mark a notice read. MARK_NOTICE_READ requires the addressed role/place and an unread notice. These are append-only authored messages, separate from derived action-inbox rows and from broadcast alerts. Referral-answer notices resolve the referring ED for ed_medical referrals; other source kinds currently have no safe referrer addressee.

machines.name: A row in the coordinator's inbox
machines.subject: Derived fact rows come from movements, stays, planned bookings and bed-meeting actions. A separate daily nobody-missed check is a commitment with append-only completion history.

states.label: Showing
states.sub: A current fact category is true, or a commitment is due. The current categories live in INBOX_CATEGORIES rather than a fixed five-item list.

states.label: Acknowledged
states.sub: Somebody has seen a fact row. The row stays exactly where it was. A commitment is never acknowledged.

states.label: Commitment completed
states.sub: The daily check can be completed and reopened. Live fact categories cannot be ticked away; bed-meeting actions use their dedicated completion event.

transitions.label: the situation becomes true
transitions.guard: nothing raises a row — it is derived, and appears on its own
hides nothing and removes nothing; a second person acknowledging is a second real fact

transitions.label: commitments only
transitions.guard: Only commitment IDs; daily-check IDs require the day-N shape, and an already-complete history refuses. A commitment is completed straight from Showing and is never acknowledged. Facts remain until their underlying situation changes.

machines.note: Acknowledgement, ownership, snoozing and completion are separate histories. Real fact rows are never completed by COMPLETE_INBOX_ITEM. The daily check uses a day-shaped identifier rather than a movement; bed-meeting actions use COMPLETE_BED_MEETING_ACTION. CANCEL_TRANSPORT appends a returned snooze and a released ownership entry to the job's awaiting-departure and booking-estimate-passed rows. Completion validates category and day syntax, not whether the day is the current day.

machines.name: A legal form's receipt
machines.subject: Whether the paperwork has physically arrived. It can be undone, and then happen again.

states.label: Recorded as received
states.sub: Any of the nine forms with a legal clock, not only 1A. A second receipt is refused. A typed received time is kept as typed and cannot be later than now.

states.label: An expiry, typed by a clinician
states.sub: Expiry comes from checked paper facts. An extension must be later; a correction with matching prior form/time/expiry and a listed reason may move it earlier. A form recorded as ended takes none unless it is a correction, and the expiry must come after the written time (M13b, M13e).

transitions.guard: three reasons: recorded in error, recorded against the wrong movement, or the form had not physically arrived

machines.note: Receipt correction appends its reason and clears the receipt without erasing history. Expiry entry need not wait for a receipt: it requires a recorded form. The admitted ward may record a typed expiry on an arrived/closed movement; a checked correction and a later extension are distinct paths.

resources.title: A ward's two bed counts
resources.blurb: The illustrated routes below show the principal stored-count changes; the current event models also cover planned admissions, direct placement and undo. A normal departure completes the named live release and raises empty/allocatable once. A departure resolving an arrival-capacity conflict clears that conflict instead of inventing another bed. Ready capacity also excludes closed wards, individually closed beds and other journeys' pending numbered reservations.

counts.name: Allocatable
counts.means: Beds the ward will let a coordinator take.

moves.note: Community order before commitment can release a hold; revocation with a held bed retains it for a person to release.
the named patient leaving, which also completes their bed release

moves.effect: + 1 on the ward they leave, − 1 on the ward they arrive at
moves.note: only a transfer recorded as arrived; the source ward's live bed release is completed in the same write
a ward's own self-report, which can put it above the empty count

counts.name: Empty
counts.means: Beds with physically nobody in them.

moves.effect: Usually −1, floored at zero; a pre-counted seeded pull is not decremented twice. An arrival with no pulled stay takes a ready bed (empty and allocatable −1) where a pull could reserve one now, or, with none ready (no empty or allocatable bed, a closed ward or closed beds, or beds held for other journeys), changes neither and is counted once, as the conflict, which names the new stay. Arrival into no empty or ready bed is recorded as a capacity conflict.

moves.note: Normally +1, bounded by authored capacity; resolving an arrival conflict or already-counted release does not create an extra free bed.

moves.effect: + 1 on the ward they leave, − 1 on the ward they arrive at
moves.note: only a transfer recorded as arrived

gates.title: Can this ward take this patient?
gates.blurb: Fourteen possible eligibility labels across two paths, not fourteen blocking checks at every step. Nine labels belong to the suitability-override list. Acuity and specialling rows are information only; their actual staffing checks occur at placement. Gender designation has no override; Ready-bed and other physical-record checks run separately.
gates.overridable: Overridable means a coordinator may proceed anyway by choosing one of five recorded reasons: the receiving team has agreed despite the mismatch; clinical urgency outweighs the mismatch; the bed information is known to be out of date; continuity with a previous admission at this unit; closer to the person's home or family.

rows.asks: If this patient is not voluntary, is the ward authorised under the Mental Health Act?
The same question, asked at the front door instead — is an authorised bed needed, and does this ward have one?
Does the ward's cohort match the patient's — adult, older adult, or youth?
The same question at the front door, asked against the age band on the referral.
Does the patient need a locked bed?
rows.note: Since 14 Nov 2026 (H9, D-210) both paths ask the same question: does the ward have locked beds at all? Whether a locked bed is free now is the referral path's separate Locked bed free check.

rows.asks: For a Secure referral at a ward with locked beds, is a locked bed free now (capped at Ready)?
rows.note: Split out of Security on the referral path (H9, D-210, 14 Nov 2026). A capacity check: a full locked side reads no bed now, never not suitable, and a recorded reason may accept a Secure referral where only open beds are free. The movement path leaves locked capacity to PULL_PATIENT.

rows.asks: Is there already an occupant of the same sex, or more than one free bed?
rows.note: Both current sex-mix paths use Ready availability (the shared Ready when the caller holds the bed records, H7), with recorded gender and the defined recorded-sex fallback for non-binary or absent gender. Do not repeat the former front-door-versus-movement capacity difference for this row.

rows.asks: Is this a forensic ward? If so it is never offered.
How long ago did the ward last confirm its numbers? A stale figure fails.
rows.note: A ward whose only failing check is an old count is still listed and can be asked, worded Bed count N min old, check with the ward (H8, D-210, 14 Nov 2026). The stale limits are unchanged.

rows.asks: Does the ward's designation suit the gender recorded at referral?
rows.note: Gender designation is checked before suitability overrides. A binary gender conflicting with the ward cannot be overridden. Non-binary, Different term and unrecorded gender can use an explicit coordinator placement record, subject to the current ward-checked reason requirements.

rows.asks: Information only: what high-acuity staffing is authored for the ward? Current use is checked at placement.
rows.note: This eligibility row always passes with info:true. PULL_PATIENT separately checks remaining high-acuity staffing and requires a valid reason plus nurse unit manager consultation for its supported exception.

rows.asks: Information only: what observation staffing is authored, and what does the recorded level need?
rows.note: This row always passes with info:true. A referral does not record observation level. PULL_PATIENT checks actual remaining observation staff; the eligibility row is not itself a hard refusal.

rows.asks: Has this ward previously declined this movement? This is historical context; the reducer does not enforce it as a suitability refusal.
Is there a bed to give?
rows.note: Movement matching can accept in principle on allocatable capacity; immediate referral matching requires the shared Ready figure Capacity prints (H7, D-210). PULL_PATIENT requires a Ready bed. Physical arrival is still recorded at zero empty capacity and creates an arrival-capacity conflict rather than refusing a patient in transit.

outside.title: Placement and held-destination checks outside the label table
outside.blurb: These checks answer physical reservations, staffing and record consistency at their actual handlers. They are not all evaluated on every path; an already-held restoration has its own checks and physical arrival has a separate record-first path.
items: A new pull needs a Ready bed, including closed-ward and closed-bed adjustments and live pulled admissions; a bed still being made ready may still be pulled (D-181 item 5). Converting a planned arrival still needs more Ready beds than pending ones. An arrival into zero empty capacity is recorded as a capacity conflict.
Every free bed still being prepared prevents converting a planned arrival, but no longer a new pull.
Current observation staff and high-acuity capacity are checked at placement; supported exceptions need their recorded facts and acuity also needs nurse unit manager consultation.
A Secure request using an open bed requires the supported recorded reason; naming an unavailable numbered reservation still refuses.
Coordinator gender-placement records are required for the cases defined by genderReviewNeeded, and a binary designation conflict has no suitability override.
A restored hold rechecks its matching admission, current staffing, legal authority and gender rather than consuming another bed.
A no-transport arrival rechecks gender/legal status before arrival; an already-moving patient is recorded without stranding them at the door.

gaps.title: The stored Unit.held field is not the live operational count
gaps.body: Operational held/closed/Ready figures are derived. Unit.held remains seed and storage-validation data, so saying it is read in zero places is false. Filling this stored field is not a way to change the live derived figure.
gaps.question: Would retiring this legacy storage field improve the model? Any removal needs a separately scoped migration and compatibility review.

gaps.title: A patient-shaped placement wrapper remains separate from the live matching path
gaps.body: genderEligibility is called by validateGenderPlacement, while live referral and movement matching share genderDesignationResult. These are distinct API shapes; the old claim that genderEligibility is never called is false. The wrapper currently has no production caller found in this source scan.
gaps.question: Should the unused wrapper be retained as a public contract or retired under a separately reviewed API change? Its existence does not mean current matching skips gender.

gaps.title: Inbox completion is for commitments; fact rows need their source condition resolved
gaps.body: The daily nobody-missed check is a completable commitment, while derived fact rows cannot be ticked away. Bed-meeting actions have a separate completion event. COMPLETE_INBOX_ITEM validates the daily-check identifier shape and appends history; it does not verify that the named day is today.
gaps.question: Should the daily-check API allow retrospective/future day records? Keep that product decision separate from the rule that live facts cannot be silenced.

review.basis: Source comparison of eleven machines, route nodes, gates, resources and current gap notes; not runtime or clinical acceptance. 5 November follow-up: explicit handler, payload, authority and caller review reconciled the consolidated audit repairs. Accepted observation sequence and legacy-tie fallback, current place/Undo provenance, safe world reset/import identity, return retry, meeting occurrence metadata and UI draft/completion ownership qualify existing transitions; they add no clinical decision or new physical transport stage. See CURRENT-REVIEW.md for the source-by-source review scope and reused versus fresh evidence. Main29f61/domain1430 reconciliation: accepted observation order is max(retained history,0)+1 with positive-safe restore metadata and sequence preserved through arrival; legacy ties retain compatibility fallback. Import and archive Undo share normalized retained identity, excluding explicit missing/privacy sentinels. Complete inverses preserve occupied-stay/leave consistency. No transition geometry or clinical rule changed; see CURRENT-REVIEW.md. #1447 consolidation, 5 November: other journeys' pending numbered bed reservations come off Ready and the free locked/open counts in the pull and planned-arrival gates; a pull release clears its held bed number and refuses a release matching no reservation; a coordinator transfer recorded as arrived needs a Ready bed; restore refuses a save whose live absences, active stays or numbered beds have more than one owner and names the broken rule. No transition geometry or clinical rule changed. 10 November (items 3, 9, 10/16/27, 26/46): escalation calls and police or ambulance crew times add record-only movement fields and events; the ward card fit lines, home team heads-up and transfer notes copy are screen reads. Cited sources compared line by line; no transition geometry or clinical rule changed. 11 November (D-141): RECORD_ARRIVAL_MODE marks an ED arrival brought by police or ambulance, a record-only movement field; the home team heads-up adds the patient's UMRN as a screen read. Cited sources compared line by line (additions only); no transition geometry or clinical rule changed. 13 November (PR C): RAISE_REFERRAL with pullBed may carry changedOnPull, kept on the pulled stage change only (restore accepts it from the fixed list); examination closures and notices name the plain outcome words; reseeds take worked examples as opt-in and place calendar-day and clock-face seed records on the board's own time. A pull no longer refuses beds still being made ready (D-181 item 5); an arrival with no pulled stay records a named occupied stay in a ready bed, or with no empty and allocatable bed is one capacity conflict (A9-08); a standing wait list answer is not a prior decline (A9-05); hold-up reasons are listed by bed state (A16-06); a ward's Undo of its own named transport-need step names that ward. Cited sources compared line by line; no transition geometry or clinical rule changed. 14 November (D-210, mechanics and clock audit): a pull, both kinds of arrival, a coordinator transfer recorded as arrived and a planned-arrival conversion record a free bed number of the kind they take (H10), and seeded stays take theirs once; the referral path's security gate no longer asks whether a locked bed is free, which is the new overridable locked_bed_free capacity check (H9); fit lists, Ask more wards and acceptance read the shared Ready (H7) and one fit classifier, so an old bed count alone stays askable (H8); a community team's yes no longer makes a ward's answer accepted elsewhere (M14(b)); withdrawing an acceptance returns that ward's referral answer to waiting (H3); a held referral bed can be released (M11, new RELEASE_REFERRAL_BED); a form recorded as ended takes no expiry, a new Form 3E ending or continuation is refused, and continuation refuses 3C after 3D and 5B on an ended 5A (M13); blank or infinite typed times are refused (L7); the worked examples are a world flag (M12); ward desks act as their own ward on bed steps (M9). Cited sources compared with main 79dc1f3cf hunk by hunk; no transition geometry changed.
